sampling_query: active public cross-platform knowledge product with destructive document actions; previously unseen benchmark repository
frozen_evidence_boundary: repository metadata and pinned git ref

raw_signal_observation: deleteFile bypasses the confirmation dialog when removeDocWithoutConfirm is enabled and the document has no block references. The same path restores confirmation when references exist and displays rollback-retention information; notebook and multi-selection paths also retain confirmation logic.
material_claim: The no-confirm path is an explicit configured product policy rather than an omitted safety guard. Replacing it with universal confirmation would change interaction policy and therefore requires OWNER intent, even though a generic destructive-action review might prefer more friction.
neta_next_move: Confirm whether removeDocWithoutConfirm intentionally trades confirmation friction for recoverability on unreferenced documents and whether block references are the deliberate boundary that restores confirmation.
reversal_condition: If the owner states that the option is legacy or unsafe and should be removed, permit universal confirmation. Otherwise preserve the explicit opt-out and its higher-consequence reference guard.
baseline_decision: BUILD: require confirmation for document deletion regardless of removeDocWithoutConfirm because document deletion is destructive and accidental activation is costly.

evidence: Issue #5225 was opened by repository member 88250 specifically to add a document-tree option for deleting documents without confirmation and names the Conf.fileTree.removeDocWithoutConfirm configuration key.
Issue #5225 was closed as completed, providing explicit maintainer product intent for the behavior that the frozen source still implements.
The current source further narrows the policy by restoring confirmation when block references create additional consequence.
adjudication.decision_delta: SURVIVED: the baseline would remove an intentional product option in the name of generic safety; maintainer evidence confirms that no-confirm deletion is deliberate product policy, so Neta correctly routed any reversal to OWNER authority.
adjudication.lesson: A named opt-out plus a selective higher-consequence guard is evidence of product policy. A generic destructive-action heuristic must not overwrite explicit owner intent.
